editorial:
Imagine getting back together with your best friends from childhood to visit a place that holds all your favorite memories. That is exactly what Saki and her four friends do when they head back to Toshimaen Amusement Park. At first, it feels like a fun trip down memory lane, but the vibe changes fast. You will feel the tension build as the group realizes that the park is not as empty as it looks. It starts with small, creepy things and quickly turns into a fight for survival. The movie does a great job of making a familiar place feel scary and wrong.

You will notice that the acting feels natural, making you actually care if the girls make it out alive. While some parts of the story move a bit slow, the scares hit hard and the twists keep you guessing. If you like J-horror with a creepy setting, you should definitely give this a try. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the dark details, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a solid pick for a weekend binge.
endingExplained: As the movie reaches its peak, you find out that the park is trapped in a loop of pain. The friends discover that their past bonds are being used against them by spirits. Most of the group does not make it out, as they are pulled into the darkness of the park. The final twist shows that the nightmare does not really end, leaving you with the feeling that the park always claims those who return.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Japanese horror and creepy abandoned places.
